data_flow.step: The native agent loop hands a canonical ToolCall (tool `Bash`, input `{command, timeout?, description?}`) to ostra_tools::execute.
execute looks up the tool's schema with defs::input_schema and calls coerce_json_strings on the input. Only stringified objects and arrays are parsed; `timeout` is not range-checked here.
execute matches `"Bash"` and calls bash::run (on Windows `PowerShell` and `Cmd` call winshell::run).
run rejects a missing or blank command, then computes timeout_ms = u64_arg(input, "timeout").unwrap_or(DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS).clamp(1, MAX_TIMEOUT_MS).
run spawns bash (sandboxed or not) in its own process tree, starts reader tasks for stdout and stderr, and pins a tokio sleep of timeout_ms as the deadline.

The select loop ends with End::TimedOut when the deadline fires first. run then calls tree.kill(), waits up to KILL_WAIT for the child, drains output for DRAIN_GRACE per read (killing the tree again if pipes stay open), restores the working directory from the pwd file, and returns ToolOutput::err("The command timed out after {timeout_ms} ms and was stopped. Output so far:\n{body}"). The message reports the clamped value, not the requested one.

patterns.description: bash::run reads `timeout` with u64_arg, falls back to DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS when it is absent or not numeric, and clamps to 1..=MAX_TIMEOUT_MS. Over-limit values are therefore silently reduced to 600000 and 0 becomes 1; neither is an error. Negative floats become 0 and then 1. A string value such as "300" yields None from u64_arg (as_u64 and as_f64 are None for strings) and silently falls back to the default. winshell::run uses the identical expression with crate::bash:: paths.
patterns.name: Timeout resolution: optional arg, default, clamp

patterns.description: A tokio sleep of timeout_ms is pinned and raced against output chunks, child exit, and cancellation. On TimedOut the process tree is killed, the child is reaped within KILL_WAIT (5 s), output is drained for DRAIN_GRACE (300 ms) per read, and the tool returns an error output with the configured timeout in the message.
patterns.name: Deadline raced in a select loop

patterns.description: The limits are not derived from the constants. The BASH description, bash_def schema, POWERSHELL, CMD, powershell_def and cmd_def each carry 120000 and/or 600000 as text. Changing a constant requires hand-editing every one of these, plus docs/internals/tools.md and HANDOVER.md. The schema has minimum 1 and maximum 600000 but no default key.
patterns.name: Limits written as literals in descriptions and schemas

patterns.description: Both existing Bash timeout tests start a background subshell that would touch a marker file after 2 s, run `sleep 30` in the foreground with an explicit timeout of 300 ms, then assert: the output is an error containing 'timed out', elapsed time is under 5 s, and the marker does not appear after waiting 2.5 s (so the process group was killed). The sandbox variant returns early when no sandbox backend is available (`sandboxed` returns None).
patterns.name: Timeout test shape

document.problem: The Bash tool's default (120000 ms) and maximum (600000 ms) timeouts are defined once as constants in bash.rs, but the same numbers are also written as literals in the tool descriptions and JSON input schemas in defs.rs and in three prose documents. The only tests that touch timeouts pass a small explicit value to prove a timeout kills the process tree; nothing tests the default, the clamp, the schema limits, or the description text.
document.scope: Task: how the Bash tool applies its default and maximum timeouts, where its description states them, and its tests. Covers the native Bash tool in crates/ostra-tools, its Windows siblings (PowerShell, Cmd) because they share the constants, and the docs that restate the numbers. Does not cover harness executors' own shell tools or the sandbox backends beyond the timeout test.
document.title: Bash tool timeouts

submit.findings_summary: bash.rs defines DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (120000) and MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (600000). run() resolves the timeout with u64_arg(...).unwrap_or(default).clamp(1, max) and races a tokio sleep against the child in a select loop. On expiry it kills the process tree and returns an error that names the clamped value. winshell.rs reuses the same constants and clamp. The limits are repeated as literals in defs.rs (BASH, POWERSHELL and CMD descriptions plus three timeout schemas with maximum 600000), in docs/internals/tools.md and in HANDOVER.md. The only timeout tests are timeout_kills_process_group and sandbox_timeout_stops_background_children in bash.rs (300 ms) and a Windows-only test in winshell.rs. Nothing tests the default, the clamp, the schema limits or the description wording.
